column1: # Source: MBMA_7603 | Guedelhoefer
# Tag: MBMA_7603_TABLES1_STRENGTHSUMMARY
# Content: Measured failure (maximum) loads of the two full-scale three-span C and Z purlin roof systems tested to failure under vacuum-simulated wind uplift (including the second
column2: induced failure of each system) and of the three in-plane deck shear tests on the Z purlin assembly.

column1: # Data basis: measured: vacuum-chamber uplift pressures at purlin buckling as stated in the narrative test descriptions and test logs; deck shear test results reported only as load-displacement curves in Fig. 60
# Units: see column headers
# Column definitions:
#   test_id = identifier assigned to each physical load test / failure event in this report
#   load_direction = direction of applied loading (uplift
#   section_type = purlin cross-section shape as printed (C or Z)
#   depth_in = nominal purlin web depth from the construction drawings
#   thickness_in = purlin base metal thickness as printed on the construction drawings
#   span_ft = nominal span length between support beams
#   n_spans = number of continuous spans in the test specimen
#   n_purlin_lines = number of parallel purlin lines in the specimen
#   panel_type = type of roof panel/deck attachment
#   bracing = bracing arrangement of the purlin top/compression flange
#   failure_load_as_printed = failure or maximum load exactly as printed in the report
#   failure_load_unit = unit of the failure load exactly as printed
#   failure_moment_as_printed = failure moment as printed (none reported)
#   failure_moment_unit = unit of the failure moment as printed
#   failure_mode = description of what limited the test
#   value_source = where in the report the value is stated (text
#   pages = PDF page number(s) where the value is stated
#   purlin_spacing_ft = center-to-center spacing of the purlin lines
#   vacuum_pressure_in_water = corresponding vacuum chamber pressure at failure as printed
#   failure_location = printed location of the buckle relative to the supports
#   tributary_width_ft = plan width of uplift pressure carried by each purlin line
#   failure_load_plf = failure load per purlin line = failure_load_as_printed (psf) x tributary_width_ft
# EXTRACTION QUALITY: ocr_repaired — only unambiguous single-character OCR fixes
# VALIDATION: 12 cells checked (AI
# TEXT SOURCE: read from page images by the model (cached transcription)

# ANOMALY FLAG: Fig. 4 prints the C-purlin web thickness as "CENTER SPAN t = 0.773" (apparently a typo/OCR artifact for 0.0773) while the exterior spans are printed as "t = .119"; C-purlin cross-section dimensions are read from the drawing on PDF page 13.
# CORRECTION (Cris Moen
column2: 2026-10-13; open question MBMA_7603-Q04): C-purlin center-span thickness taken as 0.073 in.; the printed "t = 0.773" (PDF p13
column4: as 0.773 in. is implausible for a cold-formed purlin. Exterior spans remain t = 0.119 in. as printed. Thickness column values in the C purlin rows were changed from 0.773 to 0.073.

column1: # Loading was applied as a uniform uplift (suction) pressure by evacuating a sealed timber/visqueen chamber built around the 75 ft long
column2: 6 ft 4 in. wide three-span specimens; pressures were monitored with a water manometer and checked with load cells at supports.

column1: # Purlins were spaced 5 ft apart (two purlin lines per specimen); support beams at nominal 25 ft spacing (24'-10 1/2"
# Reported loads are applied vacuum pressures in psf; the report does not state whether specimen dead load is included (dead load acts opposite to uplift).
# Z system: instrumentation was last recorded at 39 psf (Load No. 14); failure occurred while increasing load beyond that point at approximately 8.9 in. water (46.3 psf). After unloading
column2: the buckled purlin was supported by an overhead crane and the system reloaded to a second failure at 46.8 psf (Load No. 16).

column1: # C system: failure occurred while holding Load No. 34 (11.5 in. water = 59.8 psf)
column2: so all instrumentation was recorded at the failure load; a second failure was induced at about 12.4 in. water (64.5 psf) with no data recorded.

column1: # Deck shear tests (Fig. 7
column2: Fig. 60) reused a 10 ft long section cut from the mid-span of the Z purlin uplift specimen with new deck for Tests 2 and 3; results are presented only as load vs. displacement curves (axes to 4000 lb and 3.0 in.)
column3: so no numerical maximum load is printed and the failure-load cells are left empty.

column1: # Deck attachment in all tests was No. 14 self-tapping sheet metal screws through the deck into the purlin flanges (through-fastened)
column2: with bolts substituted where the deck attached to a frame beam in the shear tests.

column1: # TRIBUTARY WIDTH NOTE (Cris Moen
column2: 2026-10-27; open question MBMA_7603-Q01): tributary_width_ft = 3.167 ft per purlin = 8 in. from purlin to chamber edge + half of the 5'-0" purlin spacing
column3: from Section 1 (Typ. @ Support Beam); two purlins x 38 in. = 6'-4" sealed width (p4). By symmetry this split holds regardless of deck continuity. failure_load_plf = printed psf x 3.167 (applied vacuum load only; dead load inclusion not stated). Deck shear rows left blank.
